column2: On the authority of Abū Najīḥ al-ʿIrbāḍ ibn Sāriyah (may Allah the Exalted be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace) gave us an admonition at which our hearts trembled and our eyes shed tears. We said: “O Messenger of Allah, it is as though this were a farewell admonition, so advise us.”

He said: “I advise you to fear Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and to hear and obey, even if a slave is put in command over you. For whoever of you lives will see much disagreement. So hold to my Sunnah and the Sunnah of the rightly guided, guiding caliphs;
bite onto it with your molar teeth. And beware of newly invented matters, for every innovation is misguidance.” Reported by Abū Dāwūd and al-Tirmidhī, who said: A ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ hadith.
Waʿaẓanā (“gave us an admonition”): counselled and reminded us.
Mawʿiẓatan (“an admonition”): the tanwīn is for magnification, that is, a weighty admonition.
Wajilat (“trembled”): feared.
Minhā (“at it”): because of it.
Dharafat (“shed tears”): flowed with tears.

“It is as though this were a farewell admonition”: they understood that from his ﷺ intensity in making them fear and warning them, and thought it was because his parting from them was near; for one bidding farewell goes into a thoroughness in word and deed that others do not.
Fa-awṣinā (“so advise us”): with comprehensive, sufficient advice.
“To fear Allah”: carrying out His commands and avoiding His prohibitions.
“And to hear and obey”: those in authority. One must listen attentively to the words of the one in authority, in order to understand and know them, and one must obey him.
“Will see much disagreement”: in words, deeds and beliefs.
“So hold to my Sunnah”: keep holding fast to it. It is his ﷺ way, including the rulings of belief and practice that he established, obligatory, recommended and otherwise.
Al-rāshidīn (“the rightly guided”): those who knew the truth and followed it. What is meant by the rightly guided caliphs is Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, ʿUthmān and ʿAlī.
ʿAḍḍū (“bite”): with fatḥah on the ʿayn; ḍammah is a mistake.
Bi-l-nawājidh (“with your molar teeth”): the rearmost molars.
Bidʿah (“innovation”): what is introduced contrary to the command of the Lawgiver and to its specific or general evidence.
The printed text reads تنويها, evidently for تنوينها (“its tanwīn”).
Being intense in admonition, because it softens hearts and so makes them quicker to respond.
Relying on contextual indications in some situations, for they understood that he was bidding them farewell only from his being more intense than usual in the admonition.
One should ask the admonisher for more admonition, warning and counsel.
One of the signs of prophethood: he ﷺ foretold the great disagreement that would occur in his nation after him, and it happened so.

The command to fear Allah and to hear and obey; in this advice lies the happiness of this world and the Hereafter. As for taqwā, it is Allah's counsel to the first and the last; and as for hearing and obeying, by them the servants' interests in their livelihood are set in order and they are able to practise their religion and acts of obedience openly.
Holding fast to the Sunnah and bearing patiently the pain that befalls the one who holds fast to it; it has been said that this is what is meant by biting onto it with the molars.
When one of the rightly guided caliphs says something and someone else differs with him, following the caliph's view takes precedence.
A warning against innovating matters that have no basis in the Sharīʿah. As for what is built on the principles of the fundamentals and referred back to them,
that is neither an innovation nor misguidance.
